text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- No dispute with Saudi Arabia over sea borders, says Acting Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah. Kuwait and its Gulf ally Saudi Arabia are in the process of setting their common offshore border.
- Trade volume up 20 percent to 158 million shares on the Kuwait Stock Exchange (KSE) on Wednesday.

- Sheikh Sabah hails U.S. support to Kuwait. Washington has been Kuwait's main Western ally since the U.S.-led 1991 Gulf War ejected Iraq's troops from the tiny Gulf state after a seven-month occupation.
- About 20 billion shares worth 5.7 billion dinars ($18.9 billion) changed hands in the first half of 1997 on KSE.
- Cabinet ministers discuss audit bureau report with parliament's financial affairs committee.
- Interior Minister Sheikh Mohammad Khaled al-Sabah says Kuwait and Bahrain agreed to exchange security information.

- Parliamentary health committee to finalise health insurance scheme soon. Kuwait wants to oblige its 1.2 million foreign residents to pay an annual fee of about 50 dinars ($166) under a health insurance programme.
- Gulf Arab states seen moving closer to accord on unified tariff.
- Rise in juvenile crimes due to lapses of various sectors.
